title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (from pp. 629 and 654): G^+ is a (profinite) group containing elements ρ and σ and a central subgroup μ = {±1}. The notation suggests a profinite completion of SL2(Z) or a congruence variant: σ looks like an element with σ^2 = -1 and ρ like an elliptic element. G^+ sits with index 2 in a larger group 𝔖 = G, which also contains an 'orientation-reversing' element τ satisfying τσ = -στ and τ(ρ) = σ^{-1}(ρ^{-1}). Throughout, an element written γ(x) means conjugation of x by γ. ε_𝔖 : 𝔖 → {±1} is the sign character, playing the role of det or orientation. 𝔖^𝔤 is a normal 'geometric' subgroup with ε = 1, and 𝔖^𝔤_τ = 𝔖^𝔤 ∪ 𝔖^𝔤τ.

On p. 629 Grothendieck defines Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(G^+) × Ẑ* × μ × μ as the set of quadruples (u, μ, ε2, ε3) satisfying:
(a) u(ρ) = α(ρ) for some α ∈ 𝔖^𝔤_τ with ε(α) = ε3;
(b) the same for σ, with sign ε2;
(c) u(ε0) = ε0^μ;
(d) a normalisation condition.
The claim is that Z_{ρ,σ} is a subgroup. Conditions (b), (c), (d) clearly define subgroups. Grothendieck remarks that (a) alone probably does not, and instead shows that the locus G_{(a,b)} is stable under composition inside G_{(b)}.

This page carries out that closure argument. Take u, u' satisfying (a) and (b), with u(ρ) = α(ρ) and u'(ρ) = α'(ρ).

Case ε3 = 1. Then α lies in 𝔖^𝔤 ⊂ G^+, so u'(α) is defined, and
(u'u)(ρ) = u'(α)(u'(ρ)) = (u'(α)α')(ρ).
Hence α'' = u'(α)α' lies in 𝔖^𝔤_τ, with ε(α'') = ε'3 = ε3ε'3 (formula (7)).

Case ε3 = -1. Write α = α0τ with α0 ∈ 𝔖^𝔤. Using τ(ρ) = σ^{-1}(ρ^{-1}), we get u(ρ) = (α0σ)(ρ^{-1}), up to the central sign since σ^{-1} = -σ. Now α0σ ∈ G^+, so
(u'u)(ρ) = (u'(α0σ)α')(ρ^{-1}).
Substituting ρ^{-1} = στ(ρ) gives (u'u)(ρ) = α''(ρ) with
α'' = ε u'(α0) u'(σ) α' στ, where ε ∈ μ is free because μ is central.
The aim is to choose ε so that α'' ∈ 𝔖^𝔤_τ.

The next page finishes the argument by reducing modulo 𝔖^𝔤 and using (b) for u', namely u'(σ) ≡ ε'2 σ. This forces ε = -ε'2ε'3 and yields α'' = ε'2ε'3 u'(ατ')(α'τ'), with ε(α'') = ε(α)ε(α'). So the sign ε3 behaves multiplicatively, and Z_{ρ,σ} is a group.

The problem this serves is the 'équation des lacets' programme: describing a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group of automorphisms of a (profinite) modular-type group. These are automorphisms that send the standard generators to conjugates of themselves, possibly inverted by the orientation-reversing τ (complex conjugation). The page proves that such data are closed under composition.
errors: The text says 'Prouvons que u'u ∈ G_(a)(b) — i.e. qu'il satisfait aussi à (b)'. The condition being verified is (a), not (b); this is a slip of the pen.

The text writes α0(σ^{-1}(ρ^{-1})) = (α0σ)(ρ^{-1}). This silently replaces σ^{-1} by σ. That is harmless because σ^{-1} = -σ with -1 central, so the conjugation action is the same. The leftover sign is exactly what the free central factor ε in (8) absorbs.
The step showing α'' ∈ 𝔖^𝔤_τ is left open on this page ('si possible'). It is completed on the next page using hypothesis (b) for u'. No genuine gap.

ideas.what: Group of automorphisms of a profinite modular-type group sending the generators ρ and σ to conjugates of themselves, or of their inverses via an orientation-reversing τ, recorded by signs ε2, ε3 and a cyclotomic character μ ∈ Ẑ*
ideas.modern_name: Extended (± / complex-conjugation-including) Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group acting on the profinite completion of SL2(Z) or of mapping class groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara; Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura (GT actions on profinite modular/braid groups, 1990s)
ideas.where_published: Sketched in spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, action of Gal and 'anabelian' automorphism groups); the detailed 'équation des lacets' notes are unpublished

ideas.what: Verification that conjugacy-type conditions with a sign/orientation character compose: α'' = u'(α)α' in the orientation-preserving case, and a twisted formula with a central sign correction in the reversing case
ideas.modern_name: Closure of a subgroup defined by conjugacy conditions (a crossed-homomorphism-like composition rule)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical verification that a set of automorphisms defined by conjugacy conditions, with an orientation sign, is closed under composition. It belongs to the known 'Longue Marche' / GT-type programme and contains no new construction or connection beyond that.
transcription_corrections: 'qu'il satisfait aussi à (b)': the manuscript reads (b), but the intended condition is (a).
Line after 'Si ε3 = 1 i.e. α ∈': the target is 𝔖^𝔤, written in the margin as 𝔖^𝔤 ⊂ 𝔖^+, so u'(α) is defined. It is not 𝔖^𝔤_τ.
In (8), 'ε ∈ μ = {±1} ⇒ centre 𝔖^+' should read 'ε ∈ μ = {±1} ⊂ centre 𝔖^+'.
Last line: 'Notons que tous les facteurs du produit sont dans 𝔖^𝔤_τ 𝔖^+, en tout cas α'' ∈ 𝔖'.
